title: Isaiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who was king of Judah during the time when Rezin king of Syria and Pekah king of Israel went up to war against Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaz
questions.explanation: Ahaz was king of Judah at that time, as stated in Isaiah 7:1: 'And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah...'

questions.question: What was the result of the war against Jerusalem by Rezin and Pekah?
questions.correctAnswer: They could not prevail
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:1 says they 'went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 7, what was the relationship between Syria and Ephraim?
questions.correctAnswer: They were confederate
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:2 states 'Syria is confederate with Ephraim.'

questions.question: How was the heart of Ahaz and his people described when they heard that Syria was confederate with Ephraim?
options: Moved as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind
questions.correctAnswer: Moved as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:2 describes their hearts as 'moved, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.'

questions.question: Where was Isaiah instructed by the LORD to go to meet Ahaz?
options: At the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field
questions.correctAnswer: At the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:3 states: 'Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shearjashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field.'

questions.question: What message did Isaiah tell Ahaz to receive from the LORD?
options: Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted
questions.correctAnswer: Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:4 commands: 'Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted...'

questions.question: Who are described as 'two tails of these smoking firebrands'?
options: Rezin with Syria and the son of Remaliah
The kings of Assyria and Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Rezin with Syria and the son of Remaliah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:4 refers to 'the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.'

questions.question: What was the evil counsel taken by Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah?
options: To go up against Judah, vex it, make a breach, and set a king in the midst
questions.correctAnswer: To go up against Judah, vex it, make a breach, and set a king in the midst
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:6 says they counseled: 'Let us go up against Judah... and set a king in the midst of it.'

questions.question: What did the LORD declare about the counsel of Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son?
options: It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass
It will bring destruction to Judah
It will be delayed but succeed eventually
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:7 states: 'Thus saith the Lord GOD, It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.'

questions.question: What city is called the head of Syria in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Damascus
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:8 says: 'For the head of Syria is Damascus.'

questions.question: Within how many years did the LORD say Ephraim would be broken and cease to be a people?
questions.correctAnswer: Sixty-five years
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:8 states: 'within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken.'

questions.question: Who is described as the head of Samaria in Isaiah 7?
questions.correctAnswer: Remaliah's son
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:9 says: 'the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told Ahaz to ask a sign from Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:11 records the LORD saying: 'Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God.'

questions.question: True or False: Ahaz was willing to ask a sign from the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:12 says Ahaz replied: 'I will not ask, neither will I tempt the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said if the people would not believe, they would not be established.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:9 says: 'If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.'

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the LORD instruct Isaiah to say to Ahaz about the threat from Rezin and the son of Remaliah?
options: Take heed, be quiet, fear not, nor be fainthearted
questions.correctAnswer: Take heed, be quiet, fear not, nor be fainthearted
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:4 instructs Isaiah to tell Ahaz to be calm and not afraid of the fierce anger of Rezin and the son of Remaliah, showing God's reassurance in times of fear. This is supported by the context in Isaiah 7:1-5, which describes the threat against Judah.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 7:7, what did the Lord declare about the counsel of Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah against Judah?
options: It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass
It will be delayed but effective
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass
questions.explanation: Verse 7 clearly states that the counsel of these enemies against Judah will fail and not come to pass, emphasizing God's sovereign protection over His people, which relates to the earlier warnings and reassurances given in verses 4-6.

questions.question: What sign did the LORD offer Ahaz to confirm His promise, according to Isaiah 7:11?
options: Ask a sign from the LORD either in the depth or in the height above
Build an altar on the mountain
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a sign from the LORD either in the depth or in the height above
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:11 shows that God invited Ahaz to ask for a sign from anywhere—either the depths or the heights—to strengthen his faith, which connects to God's call for trust found in verses 10-13.

questions.question: How did Ahaz respond to the LORD's offer to ask for a sign, according to Isaiah 7:12?
options: He refused to ask, saying he would not tempt the LORD
He asked for a miraculous sign
He sought counsel from the priests
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to ask, saying he would not tempt the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 12 records Ahaz's refusal to ask for a sign, claiming he would not put God to the test, which contrasts with God's encouragement to trust and ask as seen in verses 10-11.

questions.question: What rebuke did the LORD give to the house of David in response to Ahaz's refusal in Isaiah 7:13?
options: Is it a small thing to weary men, but will you weary my God also?
You shall be destroyed for your unbelief
You must build an altar immediately
You will find strength in your own hands
questions.correctAnswer: Is it a small thing to weary men, but will you weary my God also?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:13 rebukes the house of David for testing God by refusing to trust Him, highlighting the importance of faith and obedience, which ties to the preceding verses about asking for a sign.

questions.question: What is the sign that the LORD Himself will give, as stated in Isaiah 7:14?
options: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel
A great storm will come upon the land
The enemies of Judah will be destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 prophesies a miraculous birth as a sign from God, representing His presence with His people ('Immanuel'), which is a profound encouragement for faith amid threats described earlier in the chapter.

questions.question: Why will the child eat butter and honey, according to Isaiah 7:15?
options: So that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good
Because the land is fruitful and blessed
As a symbol of peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: So that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good
questions.explanation: In verse 15, the eating of butter and honey symbolizes the child's innocence and moral development, teaching discernment between good and evil, which aligns with the sign of hope given in verse 14.

questions.question: What will happen to the land that Ahaz abhors before the child knows to refuse evil and choose good, as stated in Isaiah 7:16?
options: It shall be forsaken of both her kings
It will be restored and flourish
It will be taken by Egypt
It will remain peaceful and secure
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be forsaken of both her kings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:16 foretells that before the child matures, the land will lose its kings, indicating political upheaval and judgment, contrasting with the hopeful sign of Immanuel given in verse 14.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:17 say the LORD will bring upon Ahaz, his people, and his father's house?
options: Days that have not come since Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria
Peace and prosperity for many years
A new covenant with the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Days that have not come since Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: Verse 17 warns of unprecedented days of challenge brought by Assyria, signaling a time of trial and testing for Judah, which follows the context of judgment and political instability in previous verses.

questions.question: In Isaiah 7:18, what images does the LORD use to describe the coming judgment involving Egypt and Assyria?
options: The LORD shall hiss for the fly in Egypt and the bee in Assyria
The LORD will send locusts and hailstorms
The LORD will cause earthquakes and fire
The LORD will send lions and wolves
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall hiss for the fly in Egypt and the bee in Assyria
questions.explanation: Verse 18 uses the metaphor of a divine whistle summoning flies and bees to depict the coming invasion from Egypt and Assyria, illustrating God's control over these nations in judgment.

questions.question: How does the passage in Isaiah 7:14-16 teach about trusting God's timing and promises in difficult circumstances?
options: God provides a sign of hope (Immanuel), but judgment will precede restoration
Immediate victory is guaranteed without delay
Trust requires no signs or promises
God's promises are only for the distant future
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a sign of hope (Immanuel), but judgment will precede restoration
questions.explanation: Verses 14-16 show that while God gives a hopeful sign through Immanuel, there will be a period of hardship and judgment first, teaching believers to trust God's timing even when immediate relief is not evident.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:13-14 imply about the importance of faith in God's promises for Christian living?
options: Faith in God's promises sustains us even when circumstances are threatening
Faith is unnecessary if signs are not visible
We should rely only on political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God's promises sustains us even when circumstances are threatening
questions.explanation: The rebuke in verse 13 and the sign in verse 14 emphasize that wearying God is wrong and that trusting His promises, like the sign of Immanuel, provides strength in adversity.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 7:17, the LORD will bring unprecedented days from the time Ephraim departed from Judah, including the involvement of the king of Assyria.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:17 explicitly states that the LORD will bring days upon Ahaz and his people unlike any since Ephraim departed from Judah, involving the king of Assyria.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 7:12 shows that Ahaz eagerly asked the LORD for a sign to confirm His promises.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:12 records that Ahaz refused to ask for a sign, saying he would not tempt the LORD, showing unwillingness to seek confirmation from God.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 7:15 teaches that the child will eat butter and honey so that he may know to refuse evil and choose good, illustrating the importance of moral discernment.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states the child will eat butter and honey to learn to reject evil and choose good, highlighting the biblical virtue of moral discernment.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 7, what will happen to the land where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand silverlings?
options: It will become a vineyard again
It will be for briers and thorns
It will be a royal garden
It will be flooded and barren
questions.correctAnswer: It will be for briers and thorns
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:23 states that every place where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings will become for briers and thorns, indicating desolation and loss of value.

questions.question: In Isaiah 7, what does the Lord say he will do 'in that same day' involving a razor?
options: He will shave the king's head as a sign of mourning
He will shave with a hired razor by the king of Assyria, consuming the head, hair of feet, and beard
He will shave the priests as a symbol of purification
He will shave the soldiers to prepare them for battle
questions.correctAnswer: He will shave with a hired razor by the king of Assyria, consuming the head, hair of feet, and beard
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:20 describes the Lord shaving with a razor hired from beyond the river, specifically by the king of Assyria, symbolizing judgment upon the land.

questions.question: What is the significance of 'butter and honey' in Isaiah 7:22?
options: They represent the diet of the king
They are a sign of the land's fertility and nourishment despite hardship
questions.correctAnswer: They are a sign of the land's fertility and nourishment despite hardship
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:22 states that butter and honey will be eaten by everyone left in the land, symbolizing sustenance and provision even during difficult times.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 7:19, where will the invading peoples rest?
options: In the desolate valleys, holes of the rocks, thorns, and bushes
questions.correctAnswer: In the desolate valleys, holes of the rocks, thorns, and bushes
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:19 describes the invaders resting in desolate places such as valleys, rocks, thorns, and bushes, highlighting their widespread presence and the desolation caused.

questions.question: What will a man nourish in the day described by Isaiah 7:21?
options: A young cow and two sheep
questions.correctAnswer: A young cow and two sheep
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:21 states that in that day, a man shall nourish a young cow and two sheep, symbolizing a return to humble agrarian life amidst judgment.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 7:14 with the prophecy of a virgin conceiving?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14's prophecy of a virgin conceiving is a foreshadowing of the Messiah, as later fulfilled in the New Testament (Matthew 1:23).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the prophecy of a virgin bearing a son named Immanuel found in Isaiah 7:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 1:23
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:23 directly quotes Isaiah 7:14, identifying Jesus as 'Immanuel,' meaning 'God with us,' fulfilling the prophecy.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'Immanuel' in Isaiah 7:14?
questions.correctAnswer: God with us
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Immanuel' means 'God with us,' signifying God's presence among His people as declared in Isaiah 7:14.

questions.question: What historical context underlies the threat described in Isaiah 7:17 concerning the king of Assyria?
options: Assyria's alliance with Egypt to invade Judah
The Assyrian expansion threatening Judah after Ephraim's departure
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian expansion threatening Judah after Ephraim's departure
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:17 references the coming judgment from the king of Assyria, reflecting historical Assyrian expansion after Israel (Ephraim) was divided and weakened.

questions.question: What does the 'razor' hired by the king of Assyria symbolize in Isaiah 7:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment and destruction
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:20 uses the image of a hired razor as a metaphor for Assyria's role as God's instrument of judgment against Judah.

questions.question: Which verse in Isaiah 7 warns Ahaz not to fear or be fainthearted because of Rezin and the son of Remaliah?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 7:4
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:4 instructs Ahaz to be quiet, not to fear or fainthearted despite the threats from Rezin and the son of Remaliah.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 7:9, if the people will not believe, they shall still be established.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:9 states that if the people will not believe, they shall not be established, emphasizing the importance of faith.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 7:25 says that even on hills dug with a mattock, there will be no fear of briers and thorns because they will be used for grazing cattle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:25 explains that on hills dug with a mattock, there will be no fear of briers and thorns because the land will be used for sending forth oxen and treading of lesser cattle.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage connects to the theme of God’s presence with His people as in Isaiah 7:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 3:12
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:12 records God's promise 'I will be with thee,' paralleling the 'Immanuel' theme of God's presence in Isaiah 7:14.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'two tails of these smoking firebrands' in Isaiah 7:4 metaphorically refer to?
options: The two kings threatening Judah: Rezin and Pekah
The two armies of Egypt and Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The two kings threatening Judah: Rezin and Pekah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:4 uses the metaphor 'two tails of these smoking firebrands' to represent the fierce anger and threat posed by Rezin of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah of Israel.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:1 indicate about the military situation involving Judah?
options: Rezin and Pekah could not prevail against Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Rezin and Pekah could not prevail against Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:1 states that Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah went to war against Jerusalem, but they could not prevail against it, highlighting God's protection over Judah.

questions.question: What was the emotional response of Ahaz and his people when they heard about the confederacy of Syria and Ephraim?
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts were moved
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:2 indicates that when the house of David was told about the alliance between Syria and Ephraim, their hearts were moved like trees shaken by the wind, reflecting fear and anxiety.

questions.question: What instruction did the LORD give to Isaiah regarding Ahaz?
options: To meet him with a sign
To condemn him for his actions
questions.correctAnswer: To meet him with a sign
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 7:3, the LORD instructs Isaiah to go meet Ahaz and deliver a message to him, which included reassurance and a sign from God.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 7:4, what does the LORD advise Ahaz to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Take heed and be quiet
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:4 records the LORD advising Ahaz to take heed and be quiet, instructing him not to fear or be fainthearted despite the threats from Rezin and Pekah.

questions.question: What prophetic assurance does God provide concerning the plans of Syria and Ephraim in Isaiah 7:7?
options: They will form a lasting kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be broken
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:7 states that the plans of Syria and Ephraim shall not stand or come to pass, assuring Ahaz that their conspiracy will ultimately be unsuccessful.

questions.question: What does the prophecy in Isaiah 7:14 indicate about the birth of a child?
options: A child will be born to a wealthy family
A virgin shall conceive and bear a son
The child will be a warrior
questions.correctAnswer: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 reveals a significant prophecy that a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, which is a foreshadowing of the birth of Jesus Christ as Immanuel.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:15 imply about the nature of the child that will be born?
options: He will eat butter and honey
questions.correctAnswer: He will eat butter and honey
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:15 indicates that the child will eat butter and honey, which symbolizes a time of abundance and signifies the child's ability to discern good from evil.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:16 foretell about the land that Ahaz abhors?
options: It shall be forsaken of both her kings
It will become a great nation
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be forsaken of both her kings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:16 states that before the child knows to refuse evil and choose good, the land that Ahaz abhors will be forsaken of both its kings, indicating impending judgment.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 7:18, what will happen in that day related to Egypt and Assyria?
options: The LORD will hiss for the fly and the bee
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will hiss for the fly and the bee
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:18 prophesies that the LORD will call for the fly from Egypt and the bee from Assyria, symbolizing foreign nations coming to impact Judah.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:22 indicate about the condition of the land?
options: There will be abundance of milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: There will be abundance of milk and honey
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:22 mentions that due to the abundance of milk, the people will eat butter and honey, indicating a temporary provision amidst judgment.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 7:23 describe the transformation of the land?
options: It will be filled with cities
It will produce thorns and briers instead of vines
It will be a land of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It will produce thorns and briers instead of vines
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:23 describes a grim transformation where the land that once produced valuable vines will now yield only thorns and briers, signifying desolation.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Isaiah 7:24 to describe the state of the land?
options: A land of thorns and briers
questions.correctAnswer: A land of thorns and briers
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:24 states that men will come with arrows and bows because the land will become briers and thorns, illustrating the desolation and danger present in the land.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 7:25 suggest about the hills and their usage?
options: They will be used for farming
They will be filled with wealth
They will be safe for grazing cattle
questions.correctAnswer: They will be safe for grazing cattle
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:25 implies that the hills will be free from the fear of briers and thorns, indicating they will become suitable for grazing cattle, showing a glimmer of hope amidst judgment.

questions.question: What does the combination of Isaiah 7:7 and 9 teach about faith and stability?
options: Faith in God leads to prosperity
Lack of belief results in instability
questions.correctAnswer: Lack of belief results in instability
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:7 assures that conspiracies will not stand, and Isaiah 7:9 emphasizes that if they do not believe, they will not be established, teaching that faith is essential for stability.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 7:14 and 15 convey about the significance of the child?
options: He will know good and evil
He will be a ruler of nations
questions.correctAnswer: He will know good and evil
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:14 prophesies the virgin birth, while Isaiah 7:15 indicates that this child will know to refuse evil and choose good, highlighting his significant moral discernment.
